# Weather on mallard departure days (REAL data, our analysis) — auto-generated by scripts/analyze_weather.py

Data: 147 migration departures (moves > 310 km) vs 1916 days the same birds stayed; 97 juvenile
mallards GPS/satellite-tagged in North and South Dakota, 2018–2020 (S2). Same latitude band as Montana's Hi-Line and east.

| Condition | % of departure days | % of other days | Times more common on departure days |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overnight low -5 °C (23 °F) or colder | 66% | 22% | 2.9x |
| Overnight low -10 °C (14 °F) or colder | 31% | 5% | 6.6x |
| Overnight low -15 °C (5 °F) or colder | 10% | 1% | 13.0x |
| Snow on the ground (1 cm or more) | 56% | 22% | 2.6x |
| 3-day weather severity index 10 or more | 35% | 8% | 4.6x |
| Tailwind (wind index > 0) | 85% | 59% | 1.4x |

Median on departure days: low -7.3 °C, snow 1.7 cm, WSI3 7.0.
Median on stay days: low -1.5 °C, snow 0.0 cm, WSI3 -3.0.
Short regional moves (25–310 km): weather on move days ≈ stay days (difference > 1 °C: False). Local shuffles are not weather-driven; long migrations are.

Distance vs cold, simple fit on the public table: -28.7 km per 1 °C warmer (r = -0.47). The paper's
multivariable model reports 166 km farther per 1 °C colder; our one-variable fit agrees on direction, not size. Use the paper's number with that caveat.

Caveats: juveniles only; ND/SD weather stations; days are not independent (same birds). Descriptive, not a fitted model.
